scene.speaker: ingrid
scene.bubble: We're packing for the Aurora Expedition! What should we wear and what should we carry?
scene.intro: It is the first morning of the Aurora Expedition, and the lighthouse kitchen is full of open suitcases! Ingrid checks her list twice: uniform for the school photo, gloves and a scarf for the cold sea wind, and a secret pocket for the expedition money. Kili flies from room to room carrying socks in his beak — some of them are even the right ones. What do explorers wear, and what do they carry? Open your eyes: this unit is all about it!

activities.title: Read the sentences and write the words.

words.clue: When it rains, you open this so you don't get wet.
Some children wear this to school so everyone looks the same.
You wear these on your hands when it's cold.
You wear this round the top of your trousers.
A small place in your clothes where you can put money.
You carry your clothes in this when you go on holiday.

activities.title: Match the things with the parts of the body.
Listen. Ingrid is packing her suitcase. Write a word in each gap.

data.voice_note: Voces: Ingrid (niña, decidida) y Diego (niño, reportero).
data.script: Diego: Hello Ingrid! Are you ready for the expedition? … Ingrid: Almost! I'm packing my suitcase now. … Diego: What have you put in it? … Ingrid: Well, first my blue uniform, because the school photo is on Monday. … Diego: Good idea. Is it cold there? … Ingrid: Yes! So I'm carrying my gloves and a warm scarf. … Diego: What about the rain? … Ingrid: My umbrella is too big, so I'm taking my yellow coat. … Diego: And don't forget money for the museum! … Ingrid: It's safe in the small pocket of my rucksack.

data.instructions: Read the sentence and choose the correct word, like in the exam.

items.sentence: You wear this soft, long thing round your neck when the weather is cold and windy.
People carry their clothes and other things in this when they travel to another city.
You can wear this round thing on your head on a hot and sunny day at the beach.
You put these on your feet before your shoes, and they keep your feet warm in winter.
Some people wear this small, pretty thing on a finger. It is sometimes made of gold.

activities.title: Read the story about the picture. Write the missing words.

data.text: Ingrid is packing for the expedition. First she puts her blue {1} at the bottom, because the school photo is on Monday. Then she packs her warm {2} and her thick {3} for the cold days on the boat. Her money is safe in the small {4} of her rucksack. She is not taking her {5} because it is too big — her yellow coat is better for the rain. At the end, her {6} is so full that Kili has to sit on it to close it!

activities.title: Look and find the differences in the clothes shop.

data.text: Student A chooses a thing from the wordlist and describes it without saying its name. Student B guesses. Then swap. Example: "You wear these on your hands." — "Gloves!"

homework.prompt: Draw and label 5 things you wear and 3 things you carry to school. Write one sentence about each: I wear… / I carry…
